item.title: 01. Lesson: hood cleaning basics (first 10 minutes)
item.description: Your baseline first. These are the opening 10 minutes of your hood cleaning lesson, built from the Hood cleaning 101 primer and the Gwinnett fire rules guide: what the system is, who must pay, and why. Listen for: Who is forced to pay for a hood cleaning, and how often. Claim: Hood cleaning is code-forced recurring work: NFPA 96 sets the schedule and the fire marshal enforces it. https://notebook.google.com/notebook/18d4c3cb-12a1-44b2-98e0-f2d850c616a8
item.itunes:author: NotebookLM lesson, from 2 documents

item.title: 02. How a grease pumper steals accounts: be the backup
item.description: A grease trap is the underground tank that catches kitchen grease before the sewer; cities force restaurants to pump it. This Denver owner explains how he wins restaurants that already have a vendor. Listen for: How long his sales cycle is, and the one offer that wins the switch. Claim: Accounts take 6 to 8 months to win; being the emergency backup when the current vendor misses usually wins the work afterward. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUJlw_7Dsew&t=578s
item.itunes:author: Owner, Greasebusters (Denver grease trap pumping)

item.title: 03. Used cooking oil: the collector pays the restaurant
item.description: Used cooking oil, or UCO, is the spent fryer oil that becomes biodiesel and jet fuel. Jose runs a Houston pickup route and explains who pays whom, and why restaurants leave. Listen for: How much he pays per gallon, and what makes a restaurant switch collectors. Claim: Collectors pay restaurants about 2 dollars a gallon, contracts have mostly disappeared, and restaurants switch whenever a rival offers more, so accounts last about 2 to 3 years. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FXYV8FCqB4o&t=935s
item.itunes:author: Jose, owner, Buddy's Grease Service (Houston)

item.title: 04. What he wishes he knew before starting
item.description: Back to the Denver grease trap owner for the one thing he would tell himself before starting. Compare it with Austin Davis winning 30 hood locations in 60 days. Listen for: Which kind of restaurant is easiest to win, and why switching takes so long. Claim: Switching an existing vendor is slow; the easy wins are new restaurants and new tenants in old restaurant spaces, if you get the call first. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUJlw_7Dsew&t=1238s
item.itunes:author: Owner, Greasebusters (Denver grease trap pumping)

item.title: 05. Florida septic primer: the Indian River Lagoon rules
item.description: Septic baseline, part one. A University of Florida extension agent explains the state rules behind your Florida septic idea. A BMAP is a state cleanup plan for a polluted water body. Listen for: What the July 1, 2030 deadline forces every lagoon homeowner to do. Claim: Since 2024 new systems in the Indian River Lagoon area must be nitrogen reducing, and by July 1, 2030 every home there must upgrade or connect to sewer, failing or not. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u0Pshxo9H24&t=1775s
item.itunes:author: Andrea Albertin, UF IFAS Extension regional water resources agent

item.title: 06. Florida septic primer: ATUs and other ENR systems
item.description: Septic baseline, part two. ENR means enhanced nutrient reducing. The three kinds are an ATU (a tank with an air pump), an engineered PBTS, and a gravity in-ground filter. Listen for: Which type needs a pump and regular inspections, which is where recurring service revenue comes from. Claim: ATUs remove 51 to 79 percent of nitrogen versus about 30 percent for a conventional tank, but their pump means higher upkeep and required inspections. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u0Pshxo9H24&t=2062s
item.itunes:author: Andrea Albertin, UF IFAS Extension regional water resources agent

item.title: 07. 1,000 jobs booked before the year starts
item.description: Jeremy grew up pumping tanks in South Florida and opened his own company six years ago. Listen for how much of his year is booked before January, and who books it. Listen for: How many of his scheduled jobs are restaurant grease traps, and why those survive a recession. Claim: He starts each year with about 1,000 scheduled jobs; over 700 are city-mandated restaurant grease traps, including 17 KFCs pumped every 3 months. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TMzSMPg1WqQ&t=175s
item.itunes:author: Jeremy Philbeck, owner, Jeremy's Septic Service (Palm Beach County, FL)

item.title: 08. The Florida septic license and the dump rule
item.description: The entry gate for the septic idea. Jeremy explains who licenses a Florida septic contractor and what a qualifier is: a licensed person whose license a company operates under. Listen for: How many years in the trade he needed before the exam, and how a newcomer could get around that. Claim: Florida septic contractors are licensed by the Department of Health statewide, need 4 years in the trade or coursework to sit the exam, and must register per county to dump. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TMzSMPg1WqQ&t=530s
item.itunes:author: Jeremy Philbeck, owner, Jeremy's Septic Service (Palm Beach County, FL)

item.title: 09. One truckload: 1,500 in, a third gone to dump and driver
item.description: Now the money. Jeremy walks through one 4,000 gallon truckload: what it bills, what the dump and driver cost, and why a second truck scared him. Listen for: What one truck payment costs per month, and how many 385 dollar pump-outs it takes to cover it. Claim: A load of four 385 dollar jobs bills about 1,500; the dump takes about 350 and the driver about 385; filter cleaning adds 100 a job; a new truck is about 3,000 a month. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TMzSMPg1WqQ&t=741s
item.itunes:author: Jeremy Philbeck, owner, Jeremy's Septic Service (Palm Beach County, FL)

item.title: 10. Starting with no truck, then a 100K investor loan
item.description: Last Jeremy clip: how he started without a truck by subcontracting pump-outs, then funded an 83,000 dollar refurbished truck. This is the cheapest entry path you have heard for septic. Listen for: What the investor got in return, and how fast the loan was paid off. Claim: He began repairing systems and subbing out pumping, then borrowed 100,000 from a friend over 5 years, bought the truck cash and paid it off in 3 years. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TMzSMPg1WqQ&t=1275s
item.itunes:author: Jeremy Philbeck, owner, Jeremy's Septic Service (Palm Beach County, FL)

item.title: 11. Runner-up: why grease beats septic for repeat work
item.description: Runner-up. The Denver grease owner on why a septic company should add grease traps: the same truck, but visits two to four times a year instead of every three to four years. Listen for: How often a grease customer pays versus a septic homeowner. Claim: Grease traps are serviced at least twice and usually four times a year by code, versus once every 3 to 4 years for a home septic tank. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUJlw_7Dsew&t=1399s
item.itunes:author: Owner, Greasebusters (Denver grease trap pumping)

item.title: 12. Runner-up: how a grease pumper prices a job
item.description: Runner-up. How the Denver owner prices: a flat fee under 1,000 gallons, then per gallon, and a discount for a 90-site customer. His market research trick is simple. Listen for: What he asks restaurants to show him before he bids. Claim: Flat fee for traps under 1,000 gallons, per gallon above that; he asks restaurants for their current invoice and discounts for multi-site accounts. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUJlw_7Dsew&t=969s
item.itunes:author: Owner, Greasebusters (Denver grease trap pumping)

item.title: 13. Runner-up: oil pickup versus grease trap, explained
item.description: Runner-up. A plain explanation of two restaurant services: fryer oil pickup on a schedule, and quarterly grease trap pumping with a manifest, the signed record an inspector checks. Listen for: Which of the two is legally required, and how often. Claim: Fryer oil is picked up on a schedule by volume; grease trap pumping is city-mandated, usually quarterly, with a manifest as proof for the inspector. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FXYV8FCqB4o&t=95s
item.itunes:author: Jose, owner, Buddy's Grease Service (Houston)
